name: MIPLIB 2017 open instance shs1014
description: Find a feasible solution of the MIPLIB 2017 instance shs1014 with as low an objective value as possible (a maximisation model is negated, so that lower is better for every instance). A solution is feasible when every variable bound, every row bound and the integrality of every integer variable hold within an absolute tolerance of 1e-6 on the values as they are returned; integer variables are not rounded first.

sources.locator: A Case Study of Joint Online Truck Scheduling and Inventory Management for Multiple Warehouses
Gleixner et al. (2021), MIPLIB 2017: data-driven compilation of the 6th mixed-integer programming library (benchmark paper, not evidence).
Instance pages with submitter, group, status and best known objective.

execution.interface: solve(model) -> numpy array of num_cols values, one per column. model has name, mps_path (the uncompressed MPS file), num_cols, num_rows, A (scipy CSR matrix of the rows), col_cost, col_lower, col_upper, row_lower, row_upper, integrality (bool array), offset, maximise and indicators (a list of (row, column, value): such a row has to hold only when that column equals the value; empty for most instances). Score: col_cost @ x + offset in minimisation form (negated when maximise is true), minimized; an infeasible vector is invalid.

limitations: The objective listed on the open-instances page may have been improved since 2026-11-11 (the list did not change between 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-11).
Candidates may call HiGHS through highspy; a stronger solver is a method, not a discovery by the workflow.
The starting program finds no feasible solution of this instance (HiGHS with a 30 s limit, run of 2026-11-11), so a search starts from an invalid candidate.
The record was reproduced by this task's verifier from a published solution (or an optimiser run). See VALIDITY.md.

checks: the published solution, checked by our verifier: feasible within 1e-6, objective 22671.197426918745

science_relevance.reason: The paper has joint online truck scheduling and inventory management for multiple warehouses as its main objective, the problem named on the MIPLIB page.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Schedule truck transports of pallets between warehouses so that supply is sufficient for known and stochastic demand, as an integer program (instance shs1014).
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Warehouse replenishment by truck is a real logistics problem that has to be solved online within minutes; the integer programs are very large (here several hundred thousand variables).

papers.title: A Case Study of Joint Online Truck Scheduling and Inventory Management for Multiple Warehouses
papers.task_relation: The MIPLIB instances are integer programs of the same joint scheduling and inventory problem by the same submitter; it was not checked which data snapshot they use.
papers.primary_goal: Solve a real-world problem of transporting pallets between warehouses to guarantee supply, via convex relaxation of an integer programming formulation suitable for online optimisation.
